questions.q: The radical wing of the Congress Party with Jawaharlal Nehru as one of its main leaders, founded the Independence for India League in opposition to: [1995]
questions.e: Jawaharlal Nehru and Subhash Chandra Bose as Secretaries and S. Srinivasa Iyengar as President founded the Independence for India League in 1928. This league was established to oppose the Nehru Report, as the founders demanded complete independence and a social structure for the country instead of dominion status.

questions.q: Which one of the following was an emigre communist journal of M.N. Roy? [1995]
questions.e: Communist Vanguard was an emigre Communist journal published by M.N. Roy. It served as a medium for his political thoughts while he was abroad.

questions.q: What is the correct sequence of the following events? 1️⃣ The Lucknow Pact 2️⃣ The Introduction on Dyarchy 3️⃣ The Rowlatt Act 4️⃣ The Partition of Bengal [1995]
questions.e: The correct chronological sequence is: Partition of Bengal (1905), Lucknow Pact (1916), Rowlatt Act (February 1919), and Introduction of Dyarchy under the Montford Reforms (December 1919).

questions.q: The Barrah dacoity was the first major venture of the revolutionary terrorists of the freedom movement in: [1995]
questions.e: In 1908, the Barrah Dacoity was organized by the Dacca Anushilan Samiti under the leadership of Pulin Das in East Bengal. It was a significant early action by revolutionary groups in that region.

questions.q: In 1930, Mahatma Gandhi started Civil Disobedience Movement from: [1995]
questions.e: On 12 March 1930, Gandhi started his Civil Disobedience Movement by launching the Dandi March from Sabarmati Ashram in Gujarat. He reached Dandi on 6 April 1930 to break the salt law.

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs is not correctly matched? [1995]
o: Lala Lajpat Rai-National School at Lahore
Bal Gangadhar Tilak Satya Shodhak Sabha
questions.e: Satya Shodhak Samaj was actually founded by Jyotiba Phule in 1873, not Bal Gangadhar Tilak. The other pairs regarding Jamnalal Bajaj, Dadabhai Naoroji, and Lala Lajpat Rai are correctly matched with their respective organizations or institutions.

questions.q: The Sarabandi (no tax) campaign of 1922 was led by: [1996]
questions.e: The Sarabandi (no tax) campaign of 1922 was led by Vallabhbhai Patel in Gujarat. This campaign was a significant part of the peasant movements against the British tax administration.

questions.q: Which one of the following first mooted the idea of a constituent assembly to frame a constitution for India? [1996]
questions.e: The idea of a Constituent Assembly to frame a constitution for India was first mooted by the Swaraj Party in 1934. The Swaraj Party itself had been formed earlier in 1923 by C.R. Das and Motilal Nehru.

questions.q: Given below are two statements, one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other labelled as Reason (R). Assertion (A): The British sovereignty continued to exist in free India. Reason (R): The British sovereign appointed the last Governor General of free India. In the context of the above two statements, which one of the following is correct? [1996]
o: A is false but R is true
Both A and R are true but R is not a correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
Both A and R are true but R is the correct explanation of A
questions.e: Assertion A is false because British sovereignty ceased to exist in India after August 15, 1947, when India became independent. However, Reason R is true as the British sovereign did appoint the last Governor General of free India (Lord Mountbatten) during the transition.

questions.q: Who among the following leaders did not believe in the drain theory of Dadabhai Naoroji? [1996]
questions.e: The "drain theory," which explained the economic exploitation of India by the British, was put forward by Dadabhai Naoroji in his book "Poverty and Un-British Rule in India." Sir Syed Ahmed Khan was a leader who did not believe in this theory.

questions.q: B.R. Ambedkar was elected to the Constituent Assembly from: [1996]
questions.e: Although B.R. Ambedkar was a resident of the Bombay Presidency, he was elected to the Constituent Assembly from West Bengal.

questions.q: The Anarchical and Revolutionary Crime Act (1919) was popularly known as the: [1996]
questions.e: The Anarchical and Revolutionary Crime Act of 1919 was popularly known as the Rowlatt Act. Gandhiji referred to it as a "Black Act" because it allowed the government to imprison people without trial.

questions.q: The meeting of Indian and British political leaders during 1930-32 in London has often been referred to as the First, Second and Third Round Table Conferences. It would be incorrect to refer to them as such because: [1996]
o: Indian parties other than the Indian National Congress, participating in the conference represented sectional interests and not the whole of India
the Indian National Congress did not take part in two
the British Labour Party had withdrawn from the conference thereby making the proceeding of the conference partisan
It was an instance of a conference held in three session and not that of three separate conference
questions.e: The meetings are technically considered a single conference held in three separate sessions rather than three distinct conferences. Notably, the Indian National Congress did not participate in the first and third sessions.

questions.q: Who among the following was a prominent leader of the Congress Socialist Party? [1996]
questions.e: The Congress Socialist Party (CSP) was formed in 1934. Its prominent leaders included Jayaprakash Narayan, Acharya Narendra Dev, Basawon Singh, and Yogendra Shukla.

questions.q: Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer: List-I (Authors): A. Surendranath Banerjee, B. M.K. Gandhi, C. Subhash Chandra Bose, D. Lajpat Rai. List-II (Books): 1. Hind Swaraj, 2. The Indian Struggle, 3. Autobiographical Writings, 4. A Nation in Making. [1996]
questions.e: The correct matching is: Surendranath Banerjee wrote "A Nation in Making," M.K. Gandhi wrote "Hind Swaraj," Subhash Chandra Bose wrote "The Indian Struggle," and Lala Lajpat Rai wrote "Autobiographical Writings."

questions.q: Consider the following statements about Jawaharlal Nehru: 1️⃣ He was the president of the Congress Party in 1947 2️⃣ He presided over the Constituent Assembly 3️⃣ He formed the first Congress ministry in United Province before India's independence. Of these statements: [1996]
questions.e: All statements are incorrect: Acharya J.B. Kripalani was the president of the Congress in 1947, Dr. Rajendra Prasad presided over the Constituent Assembly, and G.B. Pant formed the first Congress ministry in the United Province.

questions.q: Which one of the following is not correct about the Cabinet Mission Plan? [1996]
questions.e: The Cabinet Mission Plan actually rejected the demand for a full-fledged Pakistan. It argued that a separate Pakistan would still include large non-Muslim populations (38% in the NW and 48% in the NE).

questions.q: Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer: List-I (Societies): A. Abhinav Bharat Society, B. Anushilan Samiti, C. Gadar Party, D. Swaraj Party. List-II (Leaders): 1. Sri Aurobindo Ghosh, 2. Lala Hardayal, 3. C.R. Das, 4. V.D. Savarkar. [1996]
questions.e: The correct matches are: Abhinav Bharat (1904) with V.D. Savarkar, Anushilan Samiti (1906) with Sri Aurobindo Ghosh, Gadar Party (1913) with Lala Hardayal, and Swaraj Party (1923) with C.R. Das.

questions.q: Match List I with II (Events and Results): A. Morley Minto Reforms, B. Simon Commission, C. Chauri-Chaura incident, D. Dandi March. List-II: 1. Country-wide agitation, 2. Withdrawal of a movement, 3. Communal electorates, 5. Illegal manufacture of salt. [1996]
questions.e: Morley-Minto Reforms (1909) introduced communal electorates. The Simon Commission (1927) led to country-wide agitation. The Chauri-Chaura incident (1922) led to the withdrawal of the Non-Cooperation Movement. The Dandi March (1930) involved the illegal manufacture of salt.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: The Non-Cooperation Movement led to: 1️⃣ Congress becoming a mass movement for the first time 2️⃣ Growth of Hindu-Muslims unity 3️⃣ Removal of fear of the British might from the minds of the people 4️⃣ British government's willingness to grant political concessions to Indians. Of these statements: [1996]
questions.e: The Non-Cooperation Movement (1920) significantly fostered Hindu-Muslim unity and helped remove the fear of British authority from the public. While it turned Congress into a more active organization, statement 4 is incorrect as the British were not immediately willing to grant concessions due to this movement alone.

questions.q: Who among the following suggested the winding up of the Indian National Congress after India attained independence? [1996]
questions.e: Mahatma Gandhi suggested winding up the Indian National Congress after independence, believing its primary goal—attaining freedom—had been achieved.

questions.q: Match List-I with List-II: A. Butler Committee Report, B. Hurtog Committee Report, C. Hunter Inquiry Committee Report, D. Muddiman Committee Report. List-II: 1. Jallianwala Bagh massacre, 2. Relationship between the Indian State and the Paramount Power, 3. Working of Dyarchy as laid down in the Montague-Chelmsford Reforms, 4. The growth of education in British India. [1997]
questions.e: The Butler Committee (1927) investigated the relationship between Indian states and the Paramount Power. The Hurtog Committee examined education growth. The Hunter Commission (1919) investigated the Jallianwala Bagh massacre. The Muddiman Committee looked at the working of Dyarchy.

questions.q: "A graduate at 18, professor and associate editor of the Sudharak at 20, Secretary of the Sarvajanik Sabha... President of the Indian National Congress at 39, a patriot whom Mahatma Gandhi himself regarded as his master." This is how a biographer describes: [1997]
questions.e: This description refers to Gopal Krishna Gokhale, who graduated at 18 and became President of the INC at the age of 39 in the 1905 Benaras session. Gandhi regarded him as his political mentor.

questions.q: Match List-I (Period) with List-II (Event): A. 1883, B. 1906, C. 1927, D. 1932. List-II: 1. Announcement of Communal Award, 2. Formation of the All India State Peoples Conference, 3. Foundation of Muslim League at Dacca, 4. First session of National Conference at Calcutta. [1997]
questions.e: The first session of the National Conference was in 1883. The Muslim League was founded in 1906. The All India States Peoples Conference was formed in 1927. The Communal Award was announced in 1932.

questions.q: The Poona Pact which was signed between the British Government and Mahatma Gandhi in 1932 provided for: [1997]
o: joint electorate with reservation for Harijans
creation of dominion status for India
questions.e: The Poona Pact (1932), signed by Ambedkar and others, abandoned separate electorates for the depressed classes (Harijans) in favor of joint electorates with an increased number of reserved seats in legislatures.

questions.q: Match List-I with List-II: A. Surat Split, B. Communal Award, C. All Party Convention, D. Poorna Swaraj Resolution. List-II: 1. 1929, 2. 1928, 3. 1932, 4. 1907. [1997]
questions.e: The Surat Split occurred in 1907. The Communal Award was announced in 1932. The All Party Convention took place in 1928. The Poorna Swaraj resolution was passed in 1929 at the Lahore session.

questions.q: Match List-I with List-II: A. Chittagaon Armoury raid, B. Kakori Conspiracy, C. Lahore Conspiracy, D. Ghadar Party. List-II: 1. Lala Hardayal, 2. Jatin Das, 3. Surya Sen, 4. Ram Prasad Bismil. [1997]
questions.e: Surya Sen led the Chittagong Armoury Raid. Ram Prasad Bismil was involved in the Kakori Conspiracy. Jatin Das was involved in the Lahore Conspiracy Case. Lala Hardayal was a co-founder of the Ghadar Party.

questions.q: M.C. Setalvad, B.N. Rao and Alladi Krishnaswamy Iyer were distinguished members of the: [1997]
questions.e: M.C. Setalvad, B.N. Rao, and Alladi Krishnaswamy Iyer were distinguished members of the Servants of India Society, which was founded by Gopal Krishna Gokhale in 1905.

questions.q: What is the correct sequence of the following events? 1️⃣ Tilak's Home Rule League 2️⃣ Karnagatamaru Incident 3️⃣ Mahatma Gandhi's arrival in India [1998]
questions.e: The correct sequence is: Komagata Maru (Karnagatamaru) Incident (September 1914), Mahatma Gandhi's arrival in India from South Africa (1915), and Tilak's Home Rule League (April 1916).

questions.q: Simon Commission of 1927 was boycotted because: [1998]
o: there was no Indian member in the Commission
Congress felt that the people of India are entitled to Swaraj
there were differences among the members
questions.e: The Simon Commission was boycotted by Indians primarily because all seven of its members were British (whites), and it contained no Indian representation.

questions.q: The Indian Muslims, in general, were not attracted to the Extremist movement because of: [1998]
o: influence of Sir Sayed Ahmed Khan
extremists' policy of harping on Hindu aspect
questions.e: Extremist leaders often invoked Hindu symbols and past heroes like Shivaji and Maharana Pratap to instill patriotism. This emphasis on a Hindu past meant that Indian Muslims were generally not attracted to the movement.

questions.q: Which one of the following events, was characterised by Montague as 'Preventive Murder'? [1998]
questions.e: Secretary of State Edwin Montagu characterized the Jallianwala Bagh massacre (April 13, 1919) as 'Preventive Murder'.

questions.q: What is the correct sequence of the following events? 1️⃣ The August offer 2️⃣ The I.N.A trial 3️⃣ The Quit India Movement 4️⃣ The Royal Indian Naval Ratings' Revolt. [1998]
questions.e: The sequence is: August Offer (1940), Quit India Movement (1942), INA Trial (1945), and Royal Indian Navy Ratings' Revolt (1946).

questions.q: Which one of the following defines extremist ideology during the early phase of Indian freedom movement? [1998]
o: Stimulating the production of indigenous articles by giving them preference over imported commodities
Organising coups against the British empire through military revolt
Obtaining self-government by aggressive means in place of petitions and constitutional ways
Providing national educational according to the requirements of the country
questions.e: Extremist ideology was defined by the belief in obtaining self-government through aggressive means like boycotts and strikes, rather than the "soft" constitutional petitions used by moderates.

questions.q: Which of the following pairs are correctly matched? 1️⃣ Theodore Beck: Mohammedan Anglo Oriental College, Aligarh. 2️⃣ Ilbert Bill: Ripon 3️⃣ Pherozeshah Mehta: Indian National Congress 4️⃣ Badruddin Tyabji: Muslims League [1998]
questions.e: Theodore Beck was associated with MAO College, Aligarh. Lord Ripon introduced the Ilbert Bill. Pherozeshah Mehta was a leader of the INC. Badruddin Tyabji was not associated with the Muslim League; he was the first Muslim president of the INC.

questions.q: "The Congress is tottering to its fall and one of my great ambitions while in India, is to assist it to a peaceful demise." This statement is attributed to: [1998]
questions.e: Lord Curzon, who served as Viceroy from 1899 to 1905, made this statement expressing his hope for the demise of the Indian National Congress.

questions.q: Who was the leader of the Ghaddar Party? [1998]
questions.e: The Ghadar Party was established in 1913 in San Francisco under the leadership of Lala Hardayal.

questions.q: Lord Mountbatten came to India as a Viceroy with specific instruction to: [1998]
o: persuade the Congress to accept the partition
questions.e: Although partition eventually occurred, Mountbatten initially had instructions to try and keep India united if possible.

questions.q: Assertion (A): The Khilafat movement did bring the urban Muslims into the fold of the National Movement. Reason (R): There was a predominant element of anti-imperialism in both the National and Khilafat Movement. [1998]
o: Both A and R are true but R is not a correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is the correct explanation of A
A is false but R is true
A is true but R is false
questions.e: Both statements are true. The anti-imperialist nature of both movements allowed them to converge, successfully bringing urban Muslims into the broader national struggle.

questions.q: Assertion (A): Partition of Bengal in 1905 brought to an end the moderates' role in the Indian freedom movement. Reason (R): The Surat session of Indian National Congress separated the Extremists from the Moderates. [1998]
o: Both A and R are true but R is the correct explanation of A
A is false but R is true
Both A and R are true but R is not a correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
questions.e: Assertion A is false because the role of moderates did not end with the partition of Bengal; they continued to be active and even reunited with extremists in 1916. Reason R is true as the 1907 Surat session did see the split between the two factions.

questions.q: Assertion (A): The first ever Bill to make primary education compulsory in India was rejected in 1911. Reason (R): Discontent would have increased if every cultivator could read. [1998]
o: A is false but R is true
Both A and R are true but R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not a correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
questions.e: Assertion A is incorrect because the specific resolution on education policy mentioned in this context occurred in 1913, not 1911. The government refused the responsibility for compulsory education but urged provincial efforts for free elementary education.

questions.q: Assertion (A): The Congress rejected the Cripps proposals. Reason (R): The Cripps Mission consisted solely of whites. [1998]
o: Both A and R are true but R is not a correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
Both A and R are true but R is the correct explanation of A
questions.e: Congress rejected the Cripps proposals primarily because they offered dominion status instead of full independence. While it is true the mission consisted only of whites, this was not the primary reason for rejection.

questions.q: Assertion (A): Gandhi stopped the Non-Cooperation Movement in 1922. Reason (R): Violence at Chauri-Chaura led him to stop the movement. [1998]
o: A is true but R is false
Both A and R are true but R is the correct explanation of A.
A is false but R is true
Both A and R are true but R is not a correct explanation of A
questions.e: Gandhi halted the Non-Cooperation Movement in February 1922 specifically due to the violent incident at Chauri-Chaura, where a mob attacked a police station.

questions.q: When the Indian Muslims League was inducted into the interim government in 1946, Liyaqat Ali Khan was assigned the portfolio of: [1998]
questions.e: In the 1946 Interim Government, Liaquat Ali Khan of the Muslim League was assigned the Finance portfolio.

questions.q: The Indian National Congress agreed in 1947 to the partition of the country mainly because: [1947]
o: India would have otherwise lost the opportunity to attain freedom
the principal of two-Nation theory was then acceptable to them
they wanted to avoid large-scale communal riots
it was imposed by the British Government and the Congress was helpless in this regard
questions.e: Congress accepted partition primarily as a practical decision to avoid the large-scale communal violence that was devastating the country at the time.

questions.q: At the time of India's Independence, Mahatma Gandhi was: [1998]
o: a member of Congress Working Committee
the General Secretary of the Congress
not a member of the Congress
questions.e: At the time of independence in August 1947, Mahatma Gandhi was not a member of the Congress; he was in Calcutta working to end communal violence.

questions.q: 'Abinava Bharat' a secret society of revolutionaries was organised by: [1999]
questions.e: Abinava Bharat was organized as a secret revolutionary society by V.D. Savarkar in 1904.

questions.q: The most short-lived of all of the Britain's constitutional experiments in India was the: [1999]
questions.e: Comparing the time spans between major acts, the 1909 Act lasted only 10 years before being replaced by the 1919 Act, making it the most short-lived in this list.

questions.q: 'It made its proposals in May. It still wanted a united India. There was to be a Federal Union composed of British provinces'. The above quotation is related to: [1999]
questions.e: The Cabinet Mission, which reached Delhi in March 1946 and issued proposals in May 1946, suggested a Federal Union and initially aimed to keep India united.

questions.q: Which Indian nationalist leader looked upon a war between Germany and Britain as a God-sent opportunity which would enable Indians to exploit the situation to their advantage? [1999]
questions.e: Subhash Chandra Bose and other socialists saw the war as an imperialist conflict and argued that Indians should exploit the situation to gain freedom through immediate mass struggle.

questions.q: Which one of the following leaders of the Congress was totally in favour of Cabinet Mission Plan? [1999]
questions.e: Sardar Patel was noted for being totally in favor of the Cabinet Mission Plan of 1946.

questions.q: Which one of the following Indian leaders was dismissed by the British from the Indian Civil Service? [1999]
questions.e: Surendranath Banerji qualified for the ICS in 1874 but was later dismissed from his post as assistant magistrate in Sylhet due to racial discrimination.

questions.q: The term "imperial preference" was applied to the: [1999]
o: subordination of Indian interest to that of the British
preference given to British political agents over Indian princes
special privileges on British imports in India
questions.e: "Imperial Preference" referred to a system of reciprocal tariffs or trade agreements that gave special privileges to British imports within the colonies of the British Empire.

questions.q: Assertion (A): Lord Linlithgow described the August Movement of 1942 as the most serious rebellion since Sepoy Mutiny. Reason (R): There was massive upsurge of the peasantry in certain areas. [1999]
o: Both A and R are true but R is the correct explanation of A
A is false but R is true
Both A and R are true but R is not a correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
questions.e: Lord Linlithgow described the Quit India (August) Movement as the most serious revolt since 1857 because of the widespread participation and heroism of the common people, including massive peasant upsurges.

questions.q: The first venture of Gandhi in all-India politics was the: [1999]
questions.e: While Champaran was his first local success, the Rowlatt Satyagraha in 1919 is considered Gandhi's first venture in all-India level politics.

questions.q: The Congress policy of pray and petition ultimately came to an end under the guidance of: [1999]
questions.e: Bal Gangadhar Tilak criticized the moderate methods of "prayer, petition and protest" as "political mendicancy" and advocated for a more militant approach.

questions.q: Match List-I with List-II: A. Shyamji Krishna Varma, B. Madame Bhikaji Cama, C. Annie Besant, D. Aurobindo Gosh. List-II: 1. Bande Mataram, 2. Indian Sociologist, 3. The Talwar, 4. Commonwealth. [1999]
questions.e: Shyamji Krishna Varma was associated with "Indian Sociologist," Madame Cama with "The Talwar," Annie Besant with "Commonwealth," and Aurobindo Ghosh with "Bande Mataram."

questions.q: "In this instance we could not play off the Mohammedans against the Hindus." To which one of the following events did this remark of Aitchison relate? [2000]
questions.e: This remark by Aitchison, a British official, was made in reference to the Hindu-Muslim unity observed during the Revolt of 1857.

questions.q: Which one of the following is not a feature of the Government of India Act of 1935? [2000]
o: Diarchy at the Centre as well as in the provinces
questions.e: Under the 1935 Act, provincial autonomy replaced diarchy in the provinces. Diarchy was proposed at the Centre, but it did not exist in both simultaneously as a feature of that act.

questions.q: The Indian National Army (I.N.A.) came into existence in 1943 in: [2000]
questions.e: While the idea was conceived in Malaya and it initially formed in Japan in 1942, the INA as a major force came into its significant existence in 1943 in Singapore under Subhash Chandra Bose.

questions.q: As an alternative to the partition of India, Gandhiji suggested to Mountbatten that he: [2000]
o: invited Nehru and Jinnah to form the government together
invite the army to take over for some time
invited Jinnah to form the government
questions.e: To avoid partition, Gandhi suggested that Mountbatten should invite Jinnah to form the government of a united India.

questions.q: The native state of Tripura became involved in the freedom movement early in the 20th century because: [2000]
o: the tribes of the state were fiercely freedom loving
there were already some groups fighting against the kingship and its protector, the British
the Bengal revolutionaries took shelter in Tripura
the kings of Tripura were always anti-British
questions.e: Tripura's involvement began early in the 20th century because local groups were already engaged in a struggle against the monarchy and its British protectors.

questions.q: After returning from South Africa, Gandhiji launched his first successful satyagraha in: [2000]
questions.e: After returning in 1915, Gandhi's first successful Satyagraha in India was in Champaran (Bihar) in 1917, where he fought for indigo farmers.

questions.q: Match List-I with List-II: A. Chittagong Armoury Raid, B. Abhinav Bharat, C. Anushilan Samiti, D. Kuka Movement. List-II: 1. Kalpana Dutt, 2. Guru Ram Singh, 3. Vikram Damodar Savarkar, 4. Aurobindo Ghosh. [2000]
questions.e: Kalpana Dutt was associated with the Chittagong Armoury Raid. V.D. Savarkar founded Abhinav Bharat. Aurobindo Ghosh was a leader in Anushilan Samiti. Guru Ram Singh led the Kuka Movement.

questions.q: Assertion (A): Lord Linlithgo described the August Movement of 1942 as the most serious revolt after the Sepoy mutiny. Reason (R): Peasants joined the movement in large number in some places. [2000]
o: A is false but R is true
A is true but R is false
Both A and R are true but R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not a correct explanation of A
questions.e: The mass participation of people, especially large numbers of peasants, made the 1942 movement a serious threat, leading Lord Linlithgow to compare it to the 1857 revolt.

questions.q: Assertion (A): The basic weakness of the early nationalist movement lay in its narrow social base. Reason (R): It fought for the narrow interests of the social groups which joined it. [2000]
o: A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
Both A and R are true but R is not a correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is the correct explanation of A
questions.e: While the early nationalist movement did have a narrow social base, the reason is incorrect because early nationalists actually fought for the rights and interests of the common people, not just their own narrow group interests.

questions.q: While delivering the presidential address, the Congress President who advocated the introduction of Roman script for Hindi language was: [2000]
questions.e: In his 1938 presidential address at the Haripura session, Subhash Chandra Bose advocated for the use of the Roman script for the Hindi language.

questions.q: At the time of partition of India, which one of the following provinces of British India came forward with a plan for a united and independent existence? [2000]
questions.e: At the time of partition, the province of Punjab initially came forward with a proposal for maintaining a united and independent existence.

questions.q: The Balkan Plan for fragmentation of India was the brain child of: [2000]
questions.e: The Balkan Plan, which suggested transferring power to separate provinces and allowing them to choose their future, was the brainchild of Lord Mountbatten.

questions.q: Consider the following statements about the Indian National Congress: 1️⃣ Sarojini Naidu was the first woman to be the President of the Congress 2️⃣ C.R. Das was in prison when he functioned as the President of the Congress 3️⃣ The first Britisher to become the President of the Congress was Alan Octavian Hume 4️⃣ Alfred Webb was the President of the Congress in 1894. Which of these statements are correct? [2000]
questions.e: Statement 1 is false (Annie Besant was first); Statement 3 is false (A.O. Hume was the founder, but George Yule was the first British President). Statements 2 and 4 are correct: C.R. Das was in prison during his presidency (1921), and Alfred Webb presided in 1894.

questions.q: The Hunter Commission was appointed after the: [2001]
questions.e: The Hunter Commission was appointed in 1919 to investigate the Jallianwala Bagh massacre.

questions.q: Who among the following leaders proposed to adopt Complete Independence as the goal of the Congress in the Ahmedabad session of 1920? [2001]
questions.e: At the 1921 Ahmedabad session (though question says 1920), Maulana Hasrat Mohani was the one who moved the resolution in favor of complete independence.

questions.q: Who among the following organized the famous Chittagong Armoury raid? [2001]
questions.e: The Chittagong Armoury Raid in April 1930 was conducted by Surya Sen and his activists under the Indian Republican Army.

questions.q: A London branch of the All India Muslim League was established in 1908 under the presidency of: [2001]
questions.e: Syed Ameer Ali established the London branch of the Muslim League in 1908.

questions.q: Who among the following was the President of the All India States' Peoples' Conference in 1939? [2001]
questions.e: Jawaharlal Nehru served as the president of the All India States' Peoples' Conference between 1935 and 1947.

questions.q: With reference to the period of extremist nationalist movement in India with its spirit of Swadeshi, which one of the following statements in not correct? [2002]
o: Tagore preached the cult of Atmasakti, the main plank of which was social and economic regeneration of the villages
Liaquat Hussain led the Muslim peasants of Barisal in their agitation
The Bengal National College was founded in 1906 with Aurobindo as the Principal
In 1889, the scheme of national education was formulated by Satish Chandra Mukherjee
questions.e: Statement A is incorrect because Liaquat Hussain did not lead the Barisal peasant movement; that movement was related to salt breaking during the Civil Disobedience Movement.

questions.q: With reference to the Indian freedom struggle, which one of the following statements is not correct? [2002]
o: Maulana Barkataullah and Maulana Obeidullah Sindhi were among those who formed a provisional government of India in Kabul.
When the Indian National Congress was formed, Syed Ahmed Khan opposed it
The All-India Muslim League which was formed in 1906 vehemently opposed the partition of Bengal and separate electorates
Hakim Ajmal Khan was one of the leaders to start a nationalist and militant Ahrar movement
questions.e: Statement C is incorrect because the Muslim League actually supported the partition of Bengal in its early years, as it created a Muslim-majority province.

questions.q: The real intention of the British for including the princely states in the Federal Union proposed by the India Act of 1935 was to: [2002]
o: finally effect the complete political and administrative take-over of all the princely states by the British
use the princes to counter-balance the anti-imperialist doctrines of the nationalist leaders
exercise more and direct political and administrative control over the princely states
involve the princes actively in the administration of the colony
questions.e: The British intended to use the princely states as a conservative element to counter-balance the growing nationalist and anti-imperialist forces in the proposed federation.

questions.q: The President of Indian National Congress at the time of partition of India was: [2002]
questions.e: Acharya J.B. Kripalani was the President of the Indian National Congress from November 1946 to December 1947, which included the time of partition.

questions.q: With reference to colonial period of Indian history, match List-I (Person) with List-II (Event): A. Macdonald, B. Linlithgo, C. Dalhousie, D. Chelmsford. List-II: 1. Doctrine of Lapse, 2. Communal Award, 3. August Offer, 4. Dyarchy. [2002]
questions.e: Ramsay MacDonald announced the Communal Award (1932). Lord Linlithgow made the August Offer (1940). Lord Dalhousie implemented the Doctrine of Lapse. Lord Chelmsford oversaw the introduction of Dyarchy (1919).

questions.q: During the Indian freedom struggle, the Khudai Khidmatgars, also known as Red Shirts called for: [2002]
o: the adoption of communist revolution ideology for political and social reform
the Pathan regional nationalist unity and a struggle against colonialism.
the adoption of terrorist tactics and methods for terrorising and finally ousting the colonial rulers
the Union of Pakhtun tribal areas in north-west with Afghanistan
questions.e: Led by Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan, the Khudai Khidmatgars were a non-violent group that advocated for Pathan nationalist unity and struggled against British colonialism.

questions.q: Assertion (A): The effect of labour participation in the Indian nationalist upsurge of the early 1930s was weak. Reason (R): The labour leaders considered the ideology of Indian National Congress as bourgeois and reactionary. [2002]
o: Both A and R are true but R is the correct explanation of A
A is false but R is true
Both A and R are true but R is not a correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
questions.e: Labour participation was weak because many labour leaders were influenced by communist ideology, which led them to view the Congress as a bourgeois organization.

questions.q: The last opportunity to avoid the partition of India was lost with the rejection of: [2002]
questions.e: The Cabinet Mission of 1946 is considered the last major opportunity to avoid partition, but its plan was ultimately rejected by the Muslim League.

questions.q: The members of the Constituent Assembly which drafted the Constitution of India were: [2002]
o: elected by the Indian National Congress and Muslim League
elected by the Legislative Assemblies of various province
questions.e: The members of the Constituent Assembly were elected by the provincial legislative assemblies through a system of proportional representation.

questions.q: Who headed the Interim Cabinet formed in the year 1946? [2003]
questions.e: The Interim Government formed in September 1946 was headed by Jawaharlal Nehru.

questions.q: The leader of the Bardoli Satyagraha (1928) was: [2003]
questions.e: Vallabhbhai Patel led the Bardoli Satyagraha in 1928, and it was the women of Bardoli who gave him the title of "Sardar."

questions.q: Assertion (A): In 1916, Maulana Mohammad Ali and Abul Kalam Azad resigned from the Legislative Council. Reason (R): The Rowlatt Act was passed by the Government in spite of being opposed by all Indian members of the Legislative Council. [2003]
o: A is false but R is true
Both A and R are true but R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not a correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
questions.e: Assertion A is false because these leaders resigned in 1919 during the Khilafat Movement, not in 1916. Reason R is true as the Rowlatt Act of 1919 was indeed passed despite unanimous opposition from Indian members.

questions.q: With reference to the Indian freedom struggle, which one of the following statements is not correct? [2003]
o: In 1931, the Congress Session at Karachi opposed the Gandhi-Irwin Pact
The Rowlatt Act aroused a wave of popular indignation and led to the Jallianwala Bagh massacre
Bhagat Singh was one of the founders of Hindustan Republican Socialist Association
Subhas Chandra Bose formed the Forward Bloc
questions.e: Statement D is incorrect because the 1931 Karachi session actually endorsed (not opposed) the Gandhi-Irwin Pact.

questions.q: An important aspect of the Cripps Mission of 1942 was: [2003]
o: the creation of an Indian Union with Dominion status very soon after the end of Second World War
the framing of a constitution for the entire Indian Union, with no separate constitution for any province, and a Union Constitution to be accepted by all provinces
that all Indian States should join the Indian Union as a condition to consider any degree of autonomy for India

the active participation and cooperation of the Indian people, communities and political parties in the British war efforts as a condition for granting independence with full sovereign status to India after the war
questions.e: A key feature of the Cripps Mission was the proposal of an Indian Union with dominion status after the end of World War II.

questions.q: When Congress leaders condemned the Montagu-Chelmsford Report, many moderates left the party to form the: [2003]
questions.e: Following the 1918 Montagu-Chelmsford Report, moderate leaders led by Surendra Nath Banerjea left Congress to form the Indian Liberal Federation in 1919.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: Some of the main features of the Government of India Act, 1935 were the: 1️⃣ abolition of diarchy in the Governor's provinces 2️⃣ power of the Governors to veto legislative action and to legislate on their own 3️⃣ abolition of the principle of communal representation. Which of the statements given above is/are correct? [2004]
questions.e: The 1935 Act abolished diarchy in provinces and gave Governors veto powers. However, statement 3 is incorrect as communal representation was actually maintained.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ The First Session of the Indian National Congress was held in Calcutta 2️⃣ The Second Session of the Indian National Congress was held under the presidentship of Dadabhai Naoroji 3️⃣ Both Indian National Congress and Muslim League held their sessions at Lucknow in 1916 and concluded the Lucknow Pact. Which of the statements given above is/are correct? [2004]
questions.e: Statement 1 is false because the first session was in Bombay (1885). Statements 2 and 3 are correct: the second session was in Calcutta under Naoroji, and the 1916 Lucknow session saw the historic Lucknow Pact.

questions.q: Which one of the following statements is correct? [2004]
o: Jawaharlal Nehru, M.A. Jinnah and Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel were members of the Constituent Assembly of India
The First Session of the Constituent Assembly of India was held in January, 1947
The Constitution of India was adopted on 26th January, 1950
The Constituent Assembly of India was elected by the Provincial Assemblies in the year 1946
questions.e: Statement A is correct. Statement B is false (Jinnah was not a member). Statement C is false (first session was Dec 9, 1946). Statement D is false (adopted Nov 26, 1949, though it came into effect Jan 26, 1950).

questions.q: The Montagu-Chelmsford Report formed the basis of: [2004]
questions.e: The Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms (1918) formed the basis for the Government of India Act, 1919.

questions.q: During the Indian freedom struggle, who among the following proposed that Swaraj should be defined as complete independence free from all foreign control? [2004]
questions.e: Maulana Hasrat Mohani proposed this definition of Swaraj while presiding over the All India Muslim League session in 1921.

questions.q: The name of the famous person of India who returned the Knighthood conferred on him by the British Government as a token of protest against the atrocities in Punjab in 1919 was: [2004]
questions.e: Rabindranath Tagore renounced his knighthood in protest against the Jallianwala Bagh massacre of 1919.

questions.q: Consider the following events during India's freedom struggle: 1️⃣ Chauri-Chaura Outrage 2️⃣ Minto-Morley Reforms 3️⃣ Dandi March 4️⃣ Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms. Which one of the following is the correct chronological order of the events above? [2004]
questions.e: The correct order is: Minto-Morley Reforms (1909), Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms (1918), Chauri-Chaura (1922), and Dandi March (1930).

questions.q: Where were the Ghadar revolutionaries, who became active during the outbreak of the World War I based? [2005]
questions.e: The Ghadar revolutionaries were primarily based in San Francisco, which is in North America.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: On the eve of launch of Quit India Movement, Mahatma Gandhi: 1️⃣ asked the government servants to resign. 2️⃣ asked the soldiers to leave their posts. 3️⃣ asked the Princes of the Princely states to accept the sovereignty of their own people. Which of the statement given above is/are correct? [2005]
questions.e: Gandhi did not ask servants to resign or soldiers to leave; he asked servants to declare allegiance and soldiers not to fire. He did, however, ask Princes to accept their people's sovereignty.

questions.q: In which one of the following provinces was a Congress ministry not formed under the Act of 1935? [2005]
questions.e: While Congress formed ministries in Bihar, Madras, Orissa, and others, it did not form a ministry in Punjab.

questions.q: At which Congress session was the working committee authorised to launch a programme of Civil Disobedience? [2005]
questions.e: The 1929 Lahore session authorized the working committee to launch the Civil Disobedience programme.

questions.q: In October 1920, who headed a group of Indians gathered at Tashkent to set up a communist party of India? [2005]
questions.e: M.N. Roy headed the group that established a communist party in Tashkent in 1920.

questions.q: Who drafted the resolution on fundamental rights for the Karachi session of Congress in 1931? [2005]
questions.e: Although Sardar Patel presided over the session, Jawaharlal Nehru was the one who drafted the resolution on Fundamental Rights.

questions.q: Who among the following was not associated with the formation of U.P. Kisan Sabha in February 1918? [2005]
questions.e: U.P. Kisan Sabha was founded by Indra Narain Dwivedi and Gauri Shankar Misra, with support from Madan Mohan Malviya. Jawaharlal Nehru was not among the founders in 1918.

questions.q: Which of the following pairs are correctly matched? 1️⃣ Champaran: Rajendra Prasad 2️⃣ Ahmedabad Mill Workers: Morarji Desai 3️⃣ Kheda: Vallabhai Patel. [2005]
questions.e: Rajendra Prasad was associated with Champaran (1917) and Vallabhbhai Patel with Kheda (1918). Morarji Desai was not a leader in the 1918 Ahmedabad Mill strike.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ Lord Mountbatten was the Viceroy when the Shimla conference took place. 2️⃣ Indian Navy Revolt, 1946 took place when the Indian sailors in the Royal Indian Navy at Bombay and Karachi rose against the Government. Which of the statements given above is/are correct? [2005]
questions.e: Statement 1 is false (Lord Wavell was Viceroy during the 1945 Shimla Conference). Statement 2 is true regarding the 1946 Navy Revolt.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ In the First Round Table Conference, Dr. Ambedkar demanded separate electorates for the depressed classes. 2️⃣ In the Poona Act, special provisions for representation of the depressed people in the local bodies and civil services were made. 3️⃣ The Indian National Congress did not take part in the Third Round Table Conference. Which of the statements given above is/are correct? [2005]
questions.e: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Regarding statement 2, the Poona Pact focused on reserved seats in legislatures rather than local bodies and civil services specifically in that way.

questions.q: Which party was founded by Subhash Chandra Bose in the year 1939 after he broke away from the Congress? [2005]
questions.e: After leaving Congress in 1939, Subhash Chandra Bose founded the Forward Bloc.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: The Government of India Act, 1935 provided for: 1️⃣ the provincial autonomy. 2️⃣ the establishment of a Federal court. 3️⃣ all India Federation at the centre. Which of the statements given above are correct? [2005]
questions.e: All three were provisions of the 1935 Act: provincial autonomy, a federal court, and a proposed All India Federation.

questions.q: Under whose presidency was the Lahore session of the Indian Congress held in the year 1929, wherein a resolution was adopted to gain complete independence from the British? [2006]
questions.e: The 1929 Lahore session, which passed the Purna Swaraj resolution, was presided over by Jawaharlal Nehru.

questions.q: Consider the following statements about Madam Bhikaji Cama: 1️⃣ Madam Cama unfurled the National Flag at the International Socialist Conference in Paris in the year 1907. 2️⃣ Madam Cama served as private secretary to Dadabhai Naoroji. 3️⃣ Madam Cama was born to a Parsi. Which of the statement(s) given above is/are correct? [2006]
questions.e: Statement 1 is false because the conference was in Stuttgart, Germany, not Paris. Statements 2 and 3 are correct.

questions.q: Which Portfolio was held by Dr. Rajendra Prasad in the Interim Government formed in the year 1946? [2006]
questions.e: In the 1946 Interim Government, Dr. Rajendra Prasad held the Food and Agriculture portfolio.

questions.q: Assertion (A): According to the Wavell Plan, the number of Hindu and Muslim members in the Executive Council were to be equal. Reason (R): Wavell thought that this arrangement would have avoided the partition of India. [2007]
o: A is false but R is true
Both A and R are true but R is the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
Both A and R are true but R is not a correct explanation of A
questions.e: Assertion A is true regarding the Wavell Plan proposals. However, the plan did not explicitly state it was a measure to avoid partition in the way described.

questions.q: Which one of the following aroused a wave of popular indignation that led to the massacre by the British at Jallianwala Bagh? [2007]
questions.e: Protests against the Rowlatt Act, which allowed imprisonment without trial, led directly to the gathering at Jallianwala Bagh where the massacre occurred.

questions.q: At which one of the following places did Mahatma Gandhi first start his Satyagraha in India? [2007]
questions.e: Gandhi's first Satyagraha in India was in Champaran (1917) to address the plight of indigo farmers.

questions.q: The song 'Amar Sonar Bangla' written during the Swadeshi Movement of India inspired the liberation struggle of Bangladesh and was adopted as the National Anthem of Bangladesh. Who wrote this song? [2007]
questions.e: Rabindranath Tagore wrote 'Amar Sonar Bangla' in 1905, and he is the only person to have written the national anthems of two countries (India and Bangladesh).

questions.q: Who among the following rejected the title of Knighthood and refused to accept a position in the Council of the Secretary of State for India? [2008]
questions.e: Gopal Krishna Gokhale rejected knighthood and a position on the Secretary of State's Council.

questions.q: During the Indian Freedom Struggle, who of the following raised an army called 'Free Indian Legion'? [2008]
questions.e: Subhash Chandra Bose raised the "Free Indian Legion" in Germany in 1942.

questions.q: Who suggested the reconstitution of the Viceroy Executive Council in which all the Portfolios including that of War Members were to be held by the Indian leaders? [2008]
questions.e: This proposal was part of the Wavell Plan discussed at the Shimla Conference in 1945.

questions.q: Who gave a systematic critique of the moderate politics of the Indian National Congress in a series of articles entitled New Lamps for Old? [2008]
questions.e: Aurobindo Ghosh wrote the series "New Lamps for Old" in the weekly 'Induprakash' to criticize the moderate policies of Congress.

questions.q: Who among the following used the phrase 'UN-British' to criticize the English colonial control of India? [2008]
questions.e: Dadabhai Naoroji famously used the term in the title of his book "Poverty and Un-British Rule in India."

questions.q: Who was the Viceroy of India when the Rowlatt Act was passed? [2008]
questions.e: Lord Chelmsford was the Viceroy (1916-1921) when the Rowlatt Act was passed in 1919.

questions.q: Who among the following Gandhian followers was a teacher by profession? [2008]
questions.e: J.B. Kripalani was a schoolteacher and professor of English and History before fully joining the freedom movement.

questions.q: Which one of the following was a journal brought out by Abul Kalam Azad? [2008]
questions.e: Abul Kalam Azad established the newspaper "Al-Hilal" to criticize the British Raj.

questions.q: Where was the First Session of the Indian National Congress held in December 1885? [2008]
questions.e: The first session of the INC was held in Bombay in December 1885 under W.C. Banerjee.

questions.q: Who among the following wrote the poem, Subh-e Azadi? [2008]
questions.e: "Subh-e Azadi" (Dawn of Freedom) was written by Faiz Ahmed Faiz in August 1947 after partition.

questions.q: Assertion (A): The Congress Ministries in all the provinces resigned in the year 1939. Reason (R): The Congress did not accept the decision of the Viceroy to declare war against Germany in the context of the Second World War. [2008]
o: A is true but R is false
Both A and R are true but R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not a correct explanation of A
A is false but R is true
questions.e: Congress ministries resigned in 1939 to protest the Viceroy declaring India at war without consulting Indian leaders.

questions.q: In the 'Individual Satyagraha', Vinoba Bhave was chosen as the first Satyagrahi. Who was the second? [2008]
questions.e: Vinoba Bhave was the first and Jawaharlal Nehru was the second Satyagrahi chosen for the Individual Satyagraha started in 1940.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: The Cripps Proposals include the provision for 1️⃣ Full independence for India. 2️⃣ Creation of constitution-making body. Which of the statements given above is/are correct? [2009]
questions.e: The proposals offered dominion status, not full independence, though they did provide for a constitution-making body after the war.

questions.q: During the freedom struggle, Aruna Asaf Ali was a major woman organizer of underground activity in: [2009]
questions.e: Aruna Asaf Ali was a key underground organizer during the Quit India Movement of 1942.

questions.q: Who of the following Prime Ministers sent Cripps Mission to India? [2009]
questions.e: British Prime Minister Winston Churchill sent the Cripps Mission to India in 1942.

questions.q: During the Indian Freedom Struggle, why did Rowlatt Act arouse popular indignation? [2009]
o: It curbed the trade union activities
It suppressed the Indian traditional education
It authorized the government to imprison people without trial
It curtailed the freedom of religion
questions.e: The Rowlatt Act was despised because it allowed for imprisonment without trial and summary procedures.

questions.q: Which one of the following began with the Dandi March? [2009]
questions.e: The Civil Disobedience Movement officially commenced with Gandhi's Dandi March in 1930.

questions.q: With which one of the following movements is the slogan "Do or die" associated? [2009]
questions.e: Mahatma Gandhi gave the "Do or Die" call during the Quit India Movement in 1942, stating that Indians should either free the country or die in the attempt.

questions.q: Who founded the Ahmedabad Textile Labour Association? [2009]
questions.e: The Ahmedabad Textile Labour Association was founded in 1917 by Mahatma Gandhi.

questions.q: In the context of the Indian freedom struggle, 16th October 1905 is well known for? [2009]
o: The formal proclamation of Swadeshi Movement was made in Calcutta town hall
Lokmanya Tilak started Swadeshi Movement in Poona
Dadabhai Naoroji declared that the goal of Indian National Congress was Swaraj
questions.e: On 16th October 1905, the Partition of Bengal took effect; the day was observed as a day of mourning throughout Bengal with people fasting and singing Bande Mataram.

questions.q: The "Instrument of Instructions" contained in the Government of India Act, 1935 have been incorporated in the Constitution of India in the year 1950 as: [2010]
o: Conduct of business of the Government of India
Extent of executive power of State
questions.e: The Instrument of Instructions issued to Governors under the 1935 Act were incorporated into the 1950 Constitution as Directive Principles of State Policy.

questions.q: With reference to Simon Commission's recommendations, which one of the following statements is correct? [2010]
o: It proposed the setting up of interprovincial council under the home department
It recommended the creation of Indian Police Service with a provision for increased pay and allowances for British recruits as compared to Indian recruits
It recommended the replacement of diarchy with responsible government in the provinces
It suggested the abolition of bicameral legislature at the centre
questions.e: The Simon Commission recommended replacing the system of diarchy with responsible government in the provinces, a change later reflected in the 1935 Act.

questions.q: Four resolutions were passed at the famous Calcutta session of Indian National Congress in 1906. The question of either retention OR of rejection of these four resolutions became the cause of a split in Congress at the next Congress session held in Surat in 1907. Which one of the following was not one of those resolutions? [2010]
questions.e: The four resolutions passed in 1906 supported Swadeshi, Boycott, and National Education; the "Annulment of partition of Bengal" was not one of those specific formal resolutions that caused the 1907 split.

questions.q: After Quit India Movement, C. Rajagopalachari issued a pamphlet entitled "The Way Out". Which one of the following was proposed in this pamphlet? [2010]
o: Fresh elections to the Central and Provincial Legislatures to be held at the end of 1945 and a Constitution making body to be convened as soon as possible.
The establishment of a "War Advisory Council" composed of representatives of British India and the Indian States.
A solution for the constitutional deadlock.
Reconstitution of the Central Executive Council in such a way that all its members, except the Governor General and the Commander-in-Chief should be Indian leaders.
questions.e: C. Rajagopalachari's "The Way Out" (1944) proposed a formula to solve the constitutional deadlock between the Congress and the Muslim League regarding the demand for Pakistan.

questions.q: What was the immediate cause for the launch of the Swadeshi movement? [2010]
o: Death sentence pronounced on the Chapekar brothers.
The arrest and deportation of Lala Lajpat Rai and Ajit Singh and passing of the Punjab Colonization Bill
A sentence of 18 months rigorous imprisonment imposed on Lokmanya Tilak
The partition of Bengal done by Lord Curzon
questions.e: The Swadeshi movement was formally proclaimed in August 1905 as a direct response to Lord Curzon's decision to partition Bengal.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ Dr. Rajendra Prasad persuaded Mahatma Gandhi to come to Champaran to investigate the problem of the peasants. 2️⃣ Acharya J.B. Kriplani was one of Mahatma Gandhi's colleagues in his Champaran investigation. Which of the statements given above is/are correct? [2010]
questions.e: It was Raj Kumar Shukla, not Rajendra Prasad, who persuaded Gandhi to go to Champaran. J.B. Kripalani was indeed one of the colleagues who assisted Gandhi during the investigation.

questions.q: For the Karachi session of Indian National Congress in 1931 presided over by Sardar Patel, who drafted the Resolution on Fundamental Rights and Economic Programme? [2010]
questions.e: Jawaharlal Nehru drafted the historic Karachi Resolution on Fundamental Rights and the National Economic Programme, which was adopted in 1931 under the presidency of Vallabhbhai Patel.

questions.q: Who among the following were official Congress negotiators with Cripps Mission? [2010]
o: Acharya J.B. Kripalani and C. Rajagopalachari
Dr. Rajendra Prasad and Rafi Ahmed Kidwai
questions.e: Jawaharlal Nehru and Maulana Abul Kalam Azad served as the official negotiators for the Indian National Congress during the 1942 Cripps Mission.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ The "Bombay Manifesto" signed in 1936 openly opposed the preaching of socialist ideals. 2️⃣ It evoked support from a large section of business community from all across India. Which of the statements given above is/are correct? [2010]
questions.e: The 1936 Bombay Manifesto was signed by 21 businessmen who opposed Nehru’s socialist ideals as they felt such views were prejudicial to private property.

questions.q: Which one of the following observation is not true about the Quit India Movement of 1942? [2011-I]
o: It did not attract the labour class in general
It was led by Mahatma Gandhi
questions.e: While intended to be non-violent, the movement saw various instances of violence such as the burning of post offices and railway stations; additionally, the communist influence meant many labour unions did not officially participate.

questions.q: What was the reason for Mahatma Gandhi to organize a satyagraha on behalf of the peasants of Kheda? 1️⃣ The administration did not suspend the land revenue collection in spite of a drought. 2️⃣ The administration proposed to introduce permanent settlement in Gujarat. Which of the statements given above is/are correct? [2011-I]
questions.e: The Kheda Satyagraha was organized because the British government insisted on full tax collection despite a famine that had destroyed the agrarian economy.

questions.q: Mahatma Gandhi said that some of his deepest convictions were reflected in a book titled, "Unto this Last". What was the message from the book that transformed Mahatma Gandhi? [2011-I]
o: The life of celibacy and spiritual pursuit are essential for a noble life
Uplifting the oppressed and poor is the moral responsibility of an educated man
All the statements (a), (b) and (c) are correct in this context
The good of individual is contained in the good of all
questions.e: Gandhi derived the message from Ruskin's book that the good of the individual is contained in the good of all, which inspired his concept of "Sarvodaya".

questions.q: With reference to Indian freedom struggle, Usha Mehta is well-known for? [2011-I]
o: participating in the second round table conference
leading a contingent of Indian national army
running the secret congress radio in the wake of quit India movement
assisting in the formation of Interim Government under Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru
questions.e: Usha Mehta is remembered for operating the "Secret Congress Radio," an underground radio station that functioned during the 1942 Quit India Movement.

questions.q: With reference to the period of Indian freedom struggle, which of the following was/were recommended by the Nehru report? 1️⃣ Complete Independence for India. 2️⃣ Provision of fundamental rights for the people of India in the Constitution. 3️⃣ Joint electorates for reservation of seats for minorities. [2011-I]
questions.e: The Nehru Report recommended Dominion Status (not Complete Independence), a Bill of Rights (Fundamental Rights), and joint electorates instead of separate electorates.

questions.q: The Congress ministries resigned in the seven provinces in 1939, because: [2012-I]
o: the Congress could not form ministries in the other four provinces
emergence of a 'left wing' in the Congress made the working of the ministries impossible
None of the statements (a), (b) and (c) given above is correct
there were widespread communal disturbances in their provinces
questions.e: The ministries resigned in protest against Viceroy Lord Linlithgow's decision to declare India a party to World War II without consulting the Indian people.

questions.q: During Indian freedom struggle, the National Social Conference was formed. What was the reason for its formation? [2012-I]
o: Indian National Congress did not want to include social reforms in its deliberations and decided to form a separate body for such a purpose

Different social reform groups or organizations of Bengal region united to form a single body to discuss the issues of larger interest and to prepare appropriate petitions/representations to the government
Behramji Malabari and M. G. Ranade decided to bring together all the social reform groups of the country under one organization
None of the statements (a), (b) and (c) given abov...
questions.e: The National Social Conference was formed as a separate body because the Indian National Congress preferred to focus on political issues rather than social reforms in its own deliberations.

questions.q: Which of the following parties were established by Dr. B. R. Ambedkar? 1️⃣ The Peasants and Workers Party of India 2️⃣ All India Scheduled Castes Federation 3️⃣ The Independent Labour Party [2012-I]
questions.e: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar founded the Independent Labour Party and the All India Scheduled Castes Federation.

questions.q: Mahatma Gandhi undertook fast unto death in 1932, mainly because: [2012-I]
o: Ramsay Macdonald announced the Communal Award
Round Table Conference failed to satisfy Indian political aspirations
Congress and Muslim League had differences of opinion
None of the statements (a), (b) and (c) given above is correct in this context
questions.e: Gandhi launched a fast unto death in September 1932 to protest against Ramsay MacDonald’s announcement of the Communal Award, which provided separate electorates for depressed classes.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: The most effective contribution made by Dadabhai Naoroji to the cause of Indian National Movement was that he 1️⃣ exposed the economic exploitation of India by the British 2️⃣ interpreted the ancient Indian texts and restored the self-confidence of Indians 3️⃣ stressed the need for eradication of all the social evils before anything else. Which of the statements given above is/are correct? [2012-I]
questions.e: Naoroji's primary contribution was his "Drain Theory," which detailed how the British were economically exploiting India.

questions.q: The Lahore Session of the Indian National Congress (1929) is very important in history, because 1️⃣ the Congress passed a resolution demanding complete independence 2️⃣ the rift between the extremists and moderates was resolved in that Session 3️⃣ a resolution was passed rejecting the two-nation theory in that Session. Which of the statements given above is/are correct? [2012-I]
questions.e: The 1929 Lahore session is historic specifically for adopting the goal of Purna Swaraj (Complete Independence).

questions.q: Which of the following is/are the principal feature(s) of the Government of India Act, 1919? 1️⃣ Introduction of dyarchy in the executive government of the provinces 2️⃣ Introduction of separate communal electorates for Muslims 3️⃣ Devolution of legislative authority by the centre to the provinces. [2012-I]
questions.e: The 1919 Act introduced provincial dyarchy and the devolution of legislative authority. Separate electorates for Muslims were actually introduced earlier by the 1909 Act.

questions.q: The Rowlatt Act aimed at: [2012-I]
o: compulsory economic support to war efforts
imprisonment without trial and summary procedures for trial
imposition of restrictions on freedom of the press
questions.e: The Rowlatt Act empowered the British government to imprison political activists without trial and used summary procedures for legal cases.

questions.q: The demand for the Tebhaga Peasant Movement in Bengal was for: [2013-I]
o: the uprooting of Zamindari system and the end of serfdom
the reduction of the share of the landlords from one-half of the crop to one-third
the grant of ownership of land to peasants as they were the actual cultivators of the land
questions.e: The Tebhaga movement in Bengal involved sharecroppers demanding two-thirds of the produce for themselves and reducing the landlord’s share to one-third.

questions.q: Annie Besant was 1️⃣ responsible for starting the Home Rule Movement 2️⃣ once the President of the Indian National Congress 3️⃣ the founder of the Theosophical Society. [2013-I]
questions.e: Annie Besant started the Home Rule Movement and was the first woman President of the INC (1917). She was the second President of the Theosophical Society, not its founder (founded by H.S. Olcott).

questions.q: The people of India agitated against the arrival of Simon Commission because: [2013-I]
o: there was no Indian member in the Simon Commission
Simon Commission recommended the abolition of Dyarchy (Diarchy) in the Provinces
Indians never wanted the review of the working of the Act of 1919
the Simon Commission suggested the partition of the country.
questions.e: The primary reason for the protest was the total exclusion of Indians from the commission, which was seen as an insult to India's ability to decide its own constitutional future.

questions.q: Quit India Movement was launched in response to: [2013-I]
questions.e: The failure of the 1942 Cripps Mission to meet Indian demands for self-government led directly to the launch of the Quit India Movement.

questions.q: The 1929 Session of Indian National Congress is of significance in the history of the Freedom Movement because the: [2014-I]
o: attainment of Self-Government was declared as the objective of the Congress
decision to participate in the Round Table Conference in London was taken
attainment of Poorna Swaraj was adopted as the goal of the Congress
questions.e: The session is landmark because the Congress officially abandoned dominion status in favor of "Poorna Swaraj" as its ultimate goal.

questions.q: Which one of the following movements has contributed to a split in the Indian National Congress resulting in the emergence of 'moderates' and 'extremists'? [2015-I]
questions.e: Disagreements over the pace and methods of the Swadeshi Movement led to the 1907 Surat split between moderates and extremists.

questions.q: With reference to Congress Socialist Party, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ It advocated the boycott of British goods and evasion of taxes. 2️⃣ It wanted to establish the dictatorship of proletariat. 3️⃣ It advocated separate electorate for minorities and oppressed classes. Which of the statements given above is / are correct? [2015-I]
questions.e: Based on the provided context, the specific statements regarding CSP’s official platform as listed in the question are considered incorrect.

questions.q: With reference to Rowlatt Satyagraha, which of the following statements is/are correct? 1️⃣ The Rowlatt Act was based on the recommendations of the 'Sedition Committee'. 2️⃣ In Rowlatt Satyagraha, Gandhiji tried to utilize the Home Rule League. 3️⃣ Demonstrations against the arrival of Simon Commission coincided with Rowlatt Satyagraha. [2015-I]
questions.e: The Rowlatt Act was based on Justice Rowlatt’s Sedition Committee. Gandhi used Home Rule Leagues and Pan-Islamist groups to organize protests. Simon Commission arrived in 1927, long after the 1919 Satyagraha.

questions.q: Who of the following organized a march on the Tanjore coast to break the Salt Law in April 1930? [2015-I]
questions.e: C. Rajagopalachari led a salt march from Trichinopoly to Vedaranniyam on the Tanjore coast in April 1930.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ The first woman President of the Indian National Congress was Sarojini Naidu. 2️⃣ The first Muslim President of the Indian National Congress was Badruddin Tyabji. Which of the statements given above is / are correct? [2015-I]
questions.e: Annie Besant was the first woman President (1917); Sarojini Naidu was the first Indian woman President (1925). Badruddin Tyabji was the first Muslim President.

questions.q: The 'Swadeshi' and 'Boycott' were adopted as methods of struggle for the first time during the: [2016-I]
o: agitation against the Partition of Bengal
visit of the Simon Commission to India
questions.e: Swadeshi and Boycott were first adopted as widespread political tools during the 1905 anti-partition protests in Bengal.

questions.q: Who among the following was/were associated with the introduction of Ryotwari Settlement in India during the British rule? 1️⃣ Lord Cornwallis 2️⃣ Alexander Reed 3️⃣ Thomas Munro [2017-I]
questions.e: Thomas Munro and Alexander Reed were the key figures behind the Ryotwari system, while Lord Cornwallis is associated with the Permanent Settlement (1793).

questions.q: Consider the following pairs: 1️⃣ Radhakanta Deb: First President of the British Indian Association 2️⃣ Gazulu Lakshminarasu Chetty: Founder of the Madras Mahajana Sabha 3️⃣ Surendranath Banerjee: Founder of the Indian Association. Which of the above pairs is/are correctly matched? [2017-I]
questions.e: Radhakanta Deb was the first president of the British Indian Association. Surendranath Banerjee co-founded the Indian Association. Madras Mahajana Sabha was founded by others like M. Viraghavachari.

questions.q: In the context of Indian history, the principle of "Dyarchy (diarchy)" refers to: [2017-I]
o: Division of the central legislature into two houses.
Division of the subjects delegated to the provinces into two categories.
Having two sets of rulers; one in London and another in Delhi.
Introduction of double government i.e., Central and State governments.
questions.e: Dyarchy involved dividing provincial administrative subjects into two categories: "Transferred" (controlled by ministers) and "Reserved" (controlled by the Governor).

questions.q: With reference to Indian freedom struggle, consider the following events: 1️⃣ Mutiny in Royal Indian Navy 2️⃣ Quit India Movement launched 3️⃣ Second Round Table Conference. What is the correct chronological sequence of the above events? [2017-I]
questions.e: The chronological order is: Second RTC (1931), Quit India Movement (1942), and RIN Mutiny (February 1946).

questions.q: The object of the Butler Committee of 1927 was to? [2017-I]
o: Improve the relationship between the Government of India and the Indian States.
Define the jurisdiction of the Central and Provincial Governments.
Define the powers of the Secretary of State for India.
questions.e: The Butler Committee (1927) was established to examine and improve the relationship between the British Paramount Power and the various Indian Princely States.

questions.q: The Trade Disputes Act of 1929 provided for: [2017-I]
o: arbitrary powers to the management to quell industrial disputes.
a system of tribunals and a ban on strikes.
the participation of workers in the management of industries.
an intervention by the British Court in the event of a trade dispute.
questions.e: The Act imposed a tribunal system and banned strikes that were not directly related to industrial disputes or were designed to coerce the government.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ The Factories Act, 1881 was passed with a view to fix the wages of industrial workers and to allow the workers to form trade unions. 2️⃣ N.M. Lokhande was a pioneer in organizing the labour movement in British India. Which of the above statements is/are correct? [2017-I]
questions.e: The 1881 Factories Act focused on child labour and safety, not wages or unions. N.M. Lokhande was indeed a pioneer, starting the weekly Dinabandhu and the Bombay Mill-hands Association.

questions.q: He wrote biographies of Mazzini, Garibaldi, Shivaji and Shrikrishna; stayed in America for some time; and was also elected to the Central Assembly. He was: [2018-I]
questions.e: Lala Lajpat Rai wrote these biographies and spent significant time in the US, where he founded the Indian Home Rule League in 1916.

questions.q: After the Santhal Uprising subsided, what was/were the measure/measures taken by the colonial government? 1️⃣ The territories called 'Santhal Parganas' were created. 2️⃣ It became illegal for a Santhal to transfer land to a non-Santhal. Select the correct answer using the code given below: [2018-I]
questions.e: After the 1855-56 revolt, the British created the Santhal Parganas and passed the Santhal Parganas Tenancy Act to prohibit the transfer of tribal land to non-Santhals.

questions.q: Which one of the following is a very significant aspect of the Champaran Satyagraha? [2018-I]
o: Active involvement of Dalit and Tribal communities of India in the National Movement
Drastic decrease in the cultivation of plantation crops and commercial crops
Active all-India participation of lawyers, students and women in the National Movement
Joining of peasant unrest to India's National Movement
questions.e: The Champaran Satyagraha was significant because it successfully integrated the grievances of the peasantry into the broader national freedom struggle.

questions.q: In 1920, which of the following changed its name to "Swarajya Sabha"? [2018-I]
questions.e: Gandhi accepted the presidency of the Home Rule League in 1920 and changed its name to Swarajya Sabha.

questions.q: With reference to Swadeshi Movement, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ It contributed to the revival of the indigenous artisan crafts and industries. 2️⃣ The National Council of Education was established as a part of Swadeshi Movement. Which of the statements given above is/are correct? [2019-I]
questions.e: The movement promoted indigenous industries (textiles, soap, etc.) and led to the creation of the National Council of Education in 1906.

questions.q: With reference to the British colonial rule in India, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ Mahatma Gandhi was instrumental in the abolition of the system of 'indentured labour'. 2️⃣ In Lord Chelmsford's 'War Conference', Mahatma Gandhi did not support the resolution on recruiting Indians for World War. 3️⃣ Consequent upon the breaking of Salt Law by Indian people, the Indian National Congress was declared illegal by the colonial rulers. Which of the statements given above are correct? [2019-I]
questions.e: Gandhi supported recruitment at Chelmsford's conference. However, he was instrumental in ending indentured labour, and Congress was indeed declared illegal after the Salt Satyagraha began.

questions.q: With reference to Indian National Movement, consider the following pairs: 1️⃣ Sir Tej Bahadur Sapru: President, All India Liberal Federation 2️⃣ K.C. Neogy: Member, The Constituent Assembly 3️⃣ P.C. Joshi: General Secretary, Communist Party of India. Which of the pairs given above is/ are correctly matched? [2019-I]
questions.e: All pairs are correctly matched: Sapru headed the Liberal Federation, Neogy was in the Constituent Assembly, and Joshi was the General Secretary of the CPI.

questions.q: With reference to the history of India, "Ulgulan" or the Great Tumult is the description of which of the following events? [2020-I]
questions.e: "Ulgulan" refers to the great rebellion led by Birsa Munda in the late 1890s against British rule and the exploitation of tribal land.

questions.q: With reference to the book "Desher Katha" written by Sakharam Ganesh Deuskar during the freedom struggle, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ It warned against the Colonial State's hypnotic conquest of the mind. 2️⃣ It inspired the performance of swadeshi street plays and folk songs. 3️⃣ The use of 'desh' by Deuskar was in the specific context of the region of Bengal. Which of the statements given above are correct? [2020-I]
questions.e: Deuskar's book warned about British mental conquest and inspired cultural resistance; while it opposed the partition of Bengal, the overall theme was broader than just that region.

questions.q: The Gandhi-Irwin Pact included which of the following? 1️⃣ Invitation to Congress to participate in the Round Table Conference 2️⃣ Withdrawal of Ordinances promulgated in connection with the Civil Disobedience Movement 3️⃣ Acceptance of Gandhi's suggestion for enquiry into police excesses 4️⃣ Release of only those prisoners who were not charged with violence. Select the correct answer using the code given below: [2020-I]
questions.e: The 1931 pact involved Congress stopping the movement, participating in the RTC, and the release of non-violent prisoners; however, the British did not agree to an inquiry into police excesses.
